assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2012 observation of a Higgs-like boson at the LHC is the experimental completion of the Standard Model's electroweak sector and one of the clearest discoveries in the field's history. The 2013 prize recognised the theoretical mechanism; the observation itself, which required decades of detector design and analysis, has no prize. This is the type of discovery I would put at the centre of a deliberation.
assessment.attribution: Credit is the hardest part. Two large collaborations made independent discoveries, and the supplied names are the founding proposers and project leaders of ATLAS and CMS rather than the analysts or the spokespeople on the announcement date. A three-person limit cannot cover the collaboration. The three listed names span both experiments, but the balance between them and the allocation are contestable. I would want expert input on whether detector leadership is the right proxy.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature. Two independent experiments, a decade of precision coupling measurements, and no change in the basic interpretation. Recognition is arguably overdue because the theory prize was awarded in 2013.
uncertainties: Whether naming detector founders rather than the discovery-era leadership fairly represents the discovery; my recollection of each person's exact role is not independently verified.
Collaboration-scale discoveries may be judged difficult to fit within the three-person rule.
Whether the committee views the 2013 prize as having already settled the Higgs question.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and developed by Ye's group into systems with stability and accuracy at the 10^-18 level, is a decisive advance in precision measurement. It has enabled tests of relativity through gravitational redshift at the centimetre scale, searches for variations of constants and dark-matter signals, and a path to redefining the second. Originality and impact are both high.
assessment.attribution: Katori made the original magic-wavelength lattice proposal and early demonstration; Ye's group drove the strontium lattice clock to record performance and shaped many of the applications. Two names give a clean configuration. Other groups (for example the NIST and PTB teams) contributed, and the 2005 prize already covered the frequency comb, so the boundary against earlier work needs care.
assessment.maturity: Mature. Multiple independent laboratories operate lattice clocks that reproduce and exceed the early results, and the interpretation is stable. Timing is good.
uncertainties: Overlap with ion-clock work recognised in 2012 and with the 2005 frequency-comb prize.
Whether other contributors to the clock's practical realisation should be weighed against the two names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller proposed the trapped-ion quantum gate and the broader framework of using controlled atomic systems for quantum computation and quantum simulation. These ideas gave experimentalists a concrete route to quantum information processing, and later work in ions, neutral atoms and Rydberg systems follows from them. Conceptual originality and breadth are high.
assessment.attribution: The pair is a natural two-person configuration for the foundational proposals, with a long record of joint papers. The unresolved allocation is how to separate theoretical foundation from later experimental realisation, which was partly recognised in 2012; the 2022 prize on entanglement also sits nearby.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a source of experiments, with the trapped-ion gate demonstrated and quantum simulation widely implemented. Because the work is a proposal that fed many platforms, timing is reasonable but proximity to earlier prizes requires thought.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 and 2022 prizes in nearby topics.
Whether a theory-only prize is as compelling as one tied to a specific discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of the baryon acoustic peak in galaxy clustering gave a standard ruler that fixes the expansion history and has become one of the main probes of dark energy. It is a direct observation of a relic of the early plasma in the late universe, a link between early- and late-time cosmology that I find compelling.
assessment.attribution: The 2005 detections came from SDSS (Eisenstein and collaborators) and 2dFGRS (Cole and the 2dF team), with Percival on the 2dF and later combined analyses. The three names are a reasonable representation, but large survey collaborations, and the earlier theoretical groundwork by others, make the allocation unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Mature. BAO has been measured repeatedly by independent surveys (SDSS, BOSS, eBOSS, WiggleZ and more) and is consistent with the CMB. Recent DESI results suggest possible dynamical dark energy, which does not undermine the method.
uncertainties: Treatment of the early theoretical predictions of the acoustic scale and who should be credited with them.
Evolving interpretation of dark-energy constraints from BAO.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator, and its experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells, opened a large field of topological band physics. It is a prediction with clear experimental confirmation and enormous follow-on impact in condensed-matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele provided the theoretical foundation. Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental realisation, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal; the omission of that proposal and of other contributors (including the late Shoucheng Zhang) is a real allocation problem, and three-dimensional topological insulators add further credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature. Many materials and independent experiments confirm the physics. Recognition is reasonable in timing, though the 2016 prize on topological phase transitions covers adjacent ground.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe proposal and for three-dimensional topological insulators.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at magic angles and the observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene created the moire-materials field. The theory-experiment pairing is clean, and the discovery is original and widely influential.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald supplied the 2011 theory, and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experimental discovery. This is one of the cleaner three-person configurations on the list, though other experimental and theoretical groups contributed to the follow-on understanding.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably confirmed by many groups, but the field is only about eight years old and the nature of the superconductivity is not settled, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism and some of the phase diagram remain debated.
Possible preference to wait for broader consolidation of the moire field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background from pulsar-timing arrays is a new window on the universe, plausibly from supermassive black-hole binaries. As a gravity theorist, I find it important, though the discovery remains at the evidence level.
assessment.attribution: Pulsar timing arrays are intrinsically collaborative (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, CPTA, IPTA). The three names represent senior figures of different collaborations, but the supplied credit does not identify decisive individual contributions to the detection, so a fair configuration is hard to establish.
assessment.maturity: Premature in my view. The 2023 results were evidence at roughly 3-4 sigma with a source interpretation still open, and the independent confirmation and spectrum characterisation are ongoing.
uncertainties: Statistical significance and source interpretation (black-hole binaries versus new physics) are unresolved.
Whether names listed track the decisive contributions or leadership.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos by IceCube opened neutrino astronomy at PeV energies, including evidence for a source in the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane. It is a clear, new observational discovery.
assessment.attribution: The single credited name reflects Halzen's central role in conceiving and leading IceCube. Large-collaboration work, the earlier AMANDA and other efforts, and the contributions of other IceCube leaders mean the allocation is unsettled, and a one-person prize would deserve scrutiny.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is firmly established and independently supported, while source identification is still developing, so maturity is good but not complete.
uncertainties: Single-person attribution within a very large collaboration.
